nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) without IR compensation was carried out in 0.1 M ultrapure KOH to reveal OER performances. As shown in Figure 2g, CoNi NS exhibits a significantly lower onset potential and higher current density compared to its monometallic counterparts. Specifically, CoNi NS achieves a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} at an overpotential ≈50 and 80 mV lower than those of Ni and Co NS

nodes.description: Chronopotentiometry stability test in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The chronopotentiometry test in Figure S8 (Supporting Information) shows a good electrocatalytic stability of the CoNi NS.

nodes.description: Tafel slope analysis in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: In addition, the reduced Tafel slope of CoNi NS suggests more efficient charge transfer kinetics than Ni and Co NSs (Figure S9, Supporting Information).

nodes.description: Double-layer capacitance for ECSA evaluation in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The electrochemically active surface area of the catalysts, as indirectly evaluated using the double-layer capacitance as shown in Figure S10 (Supporting Information), clearly demonstrates that the enhanced OER performance stems predominantly from improved intrinsic activity rather than surface area effects.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoNi NS exhibits uniform 3D nanoflower-like morphology, Co NS shows similar nanoflower morphology, Ni NS displays irregular structures with numerous structural defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a-c presents the SEM images of the as-prepared catalysts. The CoNi NS exhibit uniform 3D nanoflower-like morphology...

nodes.characterization_summary: CoNi NS has typical ultrathin nanosheet structures with well-defined edges and smooth surfaces, indicating high specific surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM analysis in Figure 2d and Figure S3 (Supporting Information) also demonstrates that these as-prepared catalysts have typical ultrathin nanosheet structures...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping reveals uniform distribution of Ni, Co, and O elements throughout the CoNi NS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry in Figure S2 (Supporting Information) further reveals uniform distribution of Ni, Co, and O elements...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP confirms successful Ni doping in CoNi NS with Co/Ni molar ratio of approximately 2:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry in Figure S2 (Supporting Information) further reveals uniform distribution of Ni, Co, and O elements... confirming successful Ni doping with a Co/Ni molar ratio of approximately 2:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows binding energies at ≈856 eV (Ni 2p3/2) and 873.5 eV (Ni 2p1/2) for CoNi and Ni NS confirming Ni(II) species; Co 2p XPS shows peaks at ≈781.5 eV (Co 2p3/2) and 797.3 eV (Co 2p1/2) for CoNi and Co NS indicating mixed Co(II)/Co(III) valence states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e,f shows the high-resolution Ni 2p and Co 2p XPS spectra, respectively. For both CoNi and Ni NSs, the Ni 2p spectra exhibit binding energies at ≈856 eV (Ni 2p3/2) and 873.5 eV (Ni 2p1/2)... The Co 2p spectra of CoNi and Co NSs display characteristic peaks at ≈781.5 eV (Co 2p3/2) and 797.3 eV (Co 2p1/2)...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns display characteristic diffraction peaks of Co(OH)₂ and Ni(OH)₂, indicating hydroxide structures with weak signals due to thin thickness and low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the XRD patterns in Figure S6 (Supporting Information) display characteristic diffraction peaks of Co(OH)₂ and Ni(OH)₂, indicating that the main components of the as-prepared nanosheets are hydroxide structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex-situ XPS after OER at 1.7 V shows Co 2p peaks for Co(IV) at 796.2 and 780.8 eV, Co(III) at 794.8 and 779.8 eV on CoNi NS; Co(IV)/Co(III) ratio increased to 2.26 compared to 1.62 for pure Co NS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This simultaneous presence of both CoOOH and CoO2 on the catalyst surface is also supported by ex situ XPS after OER at 1.7 V. Co 2p XPS spectra in Figure S16 (Supporting Information) display peaks assigned to Co(IV) at 796.2 and 780.8 eV...
